item.title: Russia tells WHO there are no plague cases in Siberian city
item.description: GENEVA — Russian authorities told the World Health Organization (WHO) on Tuesday that it has no cases of plague in the city of Irkutsk in Siberia, where a laboratory worker at a plague research institute died last week, according to a spokesperson for the UN health agency. Moscow, which is required under global health rules to respond to WHO requests within 24 hours, previously told the WHO authorities were investigating whether pneumonic plague caused her death. "No case of this dangerous disease has been recorded in the city of Irkutsk, Russian Federation," Russian authorities said in an official response to a WHO request, read out by WHO spokesperson Christian Lindmeier at a Geneva press briefing. They also told the UN agency they have identified the people in contact with the deceased and that test results for dangerous infectious pathogens were negative. Reuters could not immediately establish if this meant that they had also tested the laboratory worker and whether they could rule out plague in her case. The Russian diplomatic mission to the UN in Geneva did not immediately respo

item.title: Shinsegae to invest $1 bil. in Paramount's Warner Bros. deal
item.description: Retail conglomerate Shinsegae Group will invest $1 billion in Paramount Skydance’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, seeking to expand its retail business into global entertainment and content. The group announced Tuesday that its real estate and development arm, Shinsegae Property, will take a $1 billion stake in the combined company, alongside investors including Skydance co-CEO David Ellison and U.S. investment firm RedBird. The deal is expected to close Tuesday (local time). The investment will give Shinsegae Group access to intellectual property from Paramount and Warner Bros., including Hollywood blockbuster franchises such as “Mission: Impossible,” “Star Trek” and “Top Gun,” as well as “Harry Potter” and “Game of Thrones.” The group said it plans to combine its retail and entertainment businesses to build a platform that brings shopping and culture together, with ambitions to become a leading content hub in Asia. “This investment will go beyond a simple equity investment and serve as a stepping stone for Shinsegae Group to diversify into a new business

item.title: Francis Halzen wins Nobel Prize in physics for work on mysterious ghost particles called neutrinos
item.description: STOCKHOLM — Francis Halzen won the Nobel Prize in physics on Tuesday for his efforts to demystify a rare group of neutrinos, tiny cosmic particles that scientists believe offer clues to how the universe evolved. “It was a great surprise and I obviously didn’t expect it,” Halzen said, speaking to the committee by phone from Italy, in a call broadcast at the news conference to announce the winner. Halzen said it was predicted before that he would win the Nobel Prize but the announcement still made him feel “strange.” “I am working on a proposal, and I hope that this prize will help getting it approved,” he said to chuckles from the audience. Halzen paved the way for a new kind of astronomy The Nobel Committee for Physics also said Halzen’s work was instrumental to the construction of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory in Antarctica. “Francis Halzen realized that the ice at the South Pole could visualize these neutrino messengers from cosmos,” committee member Eva Olsson said during the news conference. “People joined him in the quest for these neutrino messengers. item.title: N. Korea warns of 'powerful counteraction' if S. Korea intrudes 'even a millimeter' into its territory
item.description: North Korea on Tuesday warned of an "immediate and powerful counteraction" if South Korea intrudes even "a millimeter" into its territory, after Seoul signaled corresponding measures over a recent land mine blast at the inter-Korean border that it has blamed on Pyongyang. The North's foreign ministry issued the statement a day after the South's military concluded the mines planted by North Korea caused the Sept. 21 blast on the southern side of the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) that left two South Korean soldiers critically injured. The South's military also conducted a mine-clearing operation at the blast site on the same day, in coordination with the U.N. Command (UNC), which oversees the border area. "We do not care about them trying to remove the mines irrelevant to us, and we have no reason to pay heed to such farce of the ROK," the ministry said, calling South Korea by its official name, the Republic of Korea. "However, if a jackboot or a spark of fire from the ROK goes even a millimeter beyond the border to violate our territory, the border guard forces of the DPRK will take an immedia

item.title: South Korea may take North Korean mine attack issue to UN
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Tuesday that South Korea is considering calling on the United Nations to take action against North Korea for planting land mines south of the Military Demarcation Line (MDL). He made the remarks during a parliamentary audit of the foreign ministry, following the South Korean military concluding on Monday that North Korean troops had planted land mines south of the MDL in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ). The mines exploded on Sept. 21 and seriously injured several South Korean soldiers. The U.N. Command (UNC) determined that placing the mines violated the 1953 Korean Armistice Agreement. Cho said the government is considering imposing unilateral sanctions targeting North Korea, as well as sending a letter to the president of the U.N. Security Council (UNSC) to call for U.N.-level action. When asked what actions would be possible, Cho said, "If the issue is dealt with at the UNSC, it could lead to a statement by the UNSC chief or the adoption of a resolution. Or we could just send a letter or not do it at all ... We are reviewing all four options." Cho said hold

item.title: Celebrities who tried opening cafes in Korea say 'think twice'
item.description: Korea may look like a cafe lover's paradise, with coffee shops seemingly around every corner. But celebrities who have actually tried running one have a surprisingly sobering message for aspiring owners: Think twice. Singer and rapper Hanhae recently shared his own costly experience in the cafe business, while K-pop icon Lee Hyo-ri revealed that even the wildly popular Jeju cafe run by her husband, musician Lee Sang-soon, did not make as much money as its long lines might have suggested. The two discussed the realities of running a cafe on the Monday episode of JTBC's relationship reality show "Love War," after a woman featured on the program said she dreamed of opening one. Hanhae immediately tried to talk her out of it. "I've actually failed at running a cafe before, so this doesn't feel like someone else's problem," he said. Hanhae said he opened a small cafe in Seoul's Sangam-dong several years ago, selling yogurt and coffee. But competing on price proved difficult when a major franchise nearby was selling coffee for as little as 900 won ($0.64) per cup. He said the reality was a far c

item.title: Lee orders renewed discussions on possible membership to CPTPP
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung instructed the government Tuesday to start over discussions on whether South Korea should join the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) amid opposition from farmers and fishermen. Lee gave the order during the closed-door portion of a Cabinet meeting at Cheong Wa Dae, referring to the major Indo-Pacific trade agreement comprising 12 countries, including Japan, Mexico, Australia, Canada and Vietnam. Together, the member countries accounted for about 15.2 percent of global trade in 2019. "President Lee said there are opinions that the CPTPP's strategic value is important at a time of profound change in the international trade order, as well as opinions that the farming and fishing industries have great concerns," presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung said in a written briefing. item.title: One year on, Trump's Gaza plan has not stopped Israeli fire or disarmed Hamas
item.description: JERUSALEM — U.S. President Donald Trump’s year-old plan to end the Gaza war has stalled, with Israel mounting near daily attacks and occupying around two-thirds of the shattered enclave where Palestinians face dire conditions. The initial phase resulted in a ceasefire on Oct. 10, 2025, and secured the release of the last remaining hostages seized in Hamas’ 2023 attacks on Israel, along with freedom for hundreds of Palestinian prisoners and detainees held by Israel. But other goals, including disarming Hamas, securing Israeli withdrawal and rebuilding Gaza, appear far from reach. What was in the plan? The first phase of Trump’s 20-point plan included a suspension of all military operations, Israeli withdrawal from part of the enclave, hostage and prisoner releases and a surge in aid. item.title: Is crowd surfing a thing of the past in smartphone era? K-pop idol's fall raises question
item.description: Crowd surfing once depended on a sea of raised hands. These days, many of those hands are holding smartphones. That collision between an old concert ritual and modern fan culture played out at a university festival in Seoul, where Tarzzan of K-pop coed group ALLDAY PROJECT fell to the ground after leaping backward from the stage in an apparent attempt to crowd surf. ALLDAY PROJECT performed at Konkuk University on Thursday. During the set, Tarzzan suddenly threw himself toward the audience, apparently expecting fans below to catch and carry him. But many concertgoers had their phones raised to film the performance and were unable to support him as he came down. Tarzzan ultimately fell to the ground, creating an alarming moment for both the performer and those around him. Security personnel helped him back onto the stage. Tarzzan then repeatedly checked on the audience rather than immediately turning attention to himself. "Is everyone here OK? I'm sorry. Nobody got hurt, right?" he asked. item.title: Korean won rises slightly against US dollar
item.description: The Korean won rose slightly against the U.S. dollar Tuesday, despite the broad strength in the U.S. currency amid lowered expectations about a rate hike by the Federal Reserve. The won was quoted at 1,343.6 won per dollar at 3:30 p.m., up 0.4 won from the close of the previous stock trading session. With the U.S. job market reporting a slower-than-expected growth in September, expectations were reduced for the Fed to tighten its monetary policy this month. Still, rising U.S. Treasury yields remained in focus. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield surged past 5.34 percent, marking the highest level since April 2002. Foreigners sold a net 1.7 trillion won ($1.27 billion) worth of local stocks during the latest regular trading session, with the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index falling 0.89 percent to close at 6,941.39.

item.title: Chief justice calls presidential intervention in Supreme Court nominations unconstitutional
item.description: Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae said Tuesday that the president has no authority to intervene when he recommends candidates for justices of the top court, escalating a dispute with President Lee Jae Myung over the selection of a new justice. Cho made the remarks during a parliamentary audit of the Supreme Court, where he strongly defended his constitutional authority and criticized Cheong Wa Dae's demand that he nominate another candidate. "Just as the chief justice cannot interfere in the National Assembly's approval process or the president's appointment process, neither the National Assembly nor the president can interfere in the chief justice's recommendation," Cho said. He argued that such intervention would violate the constitutional division of powers among state institutions and undermine judicial independence. His remarks followed a clash between Lee and the chief justice over the justice selection that has lasted more than a month. Under Article 104 of the Constitution, a 10-member recommendation committee selects at least three candidates for Supreme Court justice. The

item.title: Police pledge stern action against threats toward actor over film controversy
item.description: Police said Tuesday it will take stern action against threats targeting actor Yoo Hae-jin, following protests outside his home over alleged historical inaccuracies in his film "The Assassin(s)." Ko Beom-seok, head of the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency, issued such a warning during a press briefing, one day after Culture Minister Choi Hui-young asked the police to enhance safety measures for those involved in the film and take stern measures. On Sunday, conservative civic groups gathered outside the actor's home in northern Seoul to criticize the movie that allegedly implies late former President Park Chung-hee's involvement in the 1974 assassination of his own wife Yuk Yeong-su. "If we determine there is a risk to Yoo's safety, we will prepare additional measures, such as stepping up patrols or providing personal protection," Ko added. Earlier Tuesday, a civic group staged a rally in central Seoul, urging local companies to cancel their advertising contracts with Yoo. Another group of protesters gathered outside Hive Media Corp. to urge the production company to apologize to the public

item.title: SK Chemicals to turn discarded banners into new banner fabric
item.description: SK Chemicals said Tuesday it will establish a regional partnership network to recycle discarded banners into new banner fabric using its depolymerization technology as part of efforts to tackle the nation’s mounting waste problem. According to the company, it has formed a banner recycling consortium with four partners — MOA and Daehan Media in the Gyeongsang region, Upcloth in the Jeolla region and the resource-circulation team of Seogwipo City on Jeju Island — to establish a regional recycling system. The partnership comes as Korea generates about 6,000 tons of discarded banners annually, with around 70 percent ending up in landfills or being incinerated, according to the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. Each of the targeted regions generates more than 1,000 metric tons of banner waste annually, according to the company. SK Chemicals will use its depolymerization technology as the core of the project, chemically breaking down plastic waste into molecular building blocks and converting it back into raw materials for producing new banner fabric. item.title: Humanoid robots take center stage as Seoul opens Smart Life Week
item.description: Inside the exhibition halls of Coex in southern Seoul on Tuesday, a bipedal humanoid robot swayed its arms to a K-pop beat. Across the room, another white robotic torso traded swift returns with a human opponent across a badminton net while robot fighters wearing oversized red and blue headgear sparred inside a miniature boxing ring. The spectacle marked the opening of Smart Life Week (SLW) 2026, a tech-driven smart city expo hosted by the Seoul Metropolitan Government. Running through Thursday under the theme “Designing Life with AI,” the exhibition brings together 529 participating firms, public institutions and city governments to showcase how artificial intelligence (AI) is shifting from digital screens into physical reality. This year’s event placed heavy emphasis on robotics and “physical AI,” which is capable of sensing, navigating and acting in physical environments alongside humans. item.description: Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan reaffirmed Tuesday that Korea would participate in the Alaska liquefied natural gas (LNG) project only if it proves to be commercially viable, saying the government has just begun reviewing the proposal. He added, however, that while poor economics had long held the project back, the Middle East war had strengthened its strategic importance. “There is no question that weak commercial reasonableness kept the project from moving forward. But the Middle East war has created new strategic value,” Kim told lawmakers during a parliamentary audit. “If the project succeeds and Korea can secure LNG from Alaska, there would clearly be strategic benefits.” He made the comments in response to a question from Rep. Choi Soo-jin of the main opposition People Power Party. item.title: [COVER STORY] Ukraine's apology over NK POWs falls short of Korea's expectation: foreign minister
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Tuesday that Ukraine sent an apology over its disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea but the message fell short of Seoul’s expectations. He said the government is considering further diplomatic actions. Cho made the remarks during a parliamentary audit of the foreign ministry amid a dispute over Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s disclosure of the transfer, which Seoul said the two sides had agreed to keep confidential. “I have been exchanging messages with the Ukrainian foreign minister, who is very troubled by the situation, and I received a message that included words of apology,” Cho told lawmakers. “But it was somewhat different from the level we had expected, so we intend to take firm measures,” he said. item.title: Egyptian president to make state visit to Korea this week
item.description: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi will make a state visit to Korea this week and hold a summit with President Lee Jae Myung on economic and international issues, Lee's office said Tuesday. At Lee's invitation, El-Sisi will arrive in Korea on Wednesday and meet with Lee Thursday during a three-day stay, presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung said in a written briefing. "Through the summit, (the two leaders) plan to hold in-depth discussions on economic cooperation, such as trade and investment, infrastructure and supply chains, as well as expanding people-to-people exchanges, the regional political situation and international issues," she said. This will be El-Sisi's first visit to the country since 2016. The two men last met in November during Lee's visit to Egypt. "We expect President El-Sisi's state visit to serve as an important opportunity to develop Korea-Egypt ties into a strategic partnership and further strengthen our country's cooperation with Africa and the Middle East," Kang said.

item.title: Busan Int'l Film Festival kicks off star-studded 10-day run
item.description: BUSAN — The 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) opened Tuesday for a 10-day run, bringing 316 films from 59 countries to Korea’s southeastern port city and ushering in an expanded set of cinema events with international prestige. The opening ceremony, hosted by actor Kim Min-ha, took place at the Busan Cinema Center, officially kicking off Asia’s largest film festival. Following the opening ceremony, director Kim Jong-kwan’s "The Table: Day and Night" will have its world premiere as the opening film. The movie explores the intersecting lives of four couples visiting a cafe during the transition from summer to autumn. Kim expressed his gratitude for the festival's spotlight on details, lauding their importance for his film, which weaves together four separate stories. "This movie is a story about small, subtle things, focusing on the meaning and beauty held within them," Kim said during a press conference at the Busan Cinema Center. "I am deeply honored and delighted to present this film on such a prestigious stage as the opening of the Busan International Film Festival.

item.title: Lotte Department Store tops $744 mil. in foreign customer sales
item.description: Lotte Department Store said its foreign customer sales nationwide surpassed 1 trillion won ($744 million) on Tuesday, making it the first Korean department store operator to reach the milestone. The retailer, which already exceeded last year's total of 734.8 billion won in July, attributed the growth to demand for luxury goods and Korean fashion, food and cultural experiences. Its Myeong-dong shopping district operations in central Seoul generated about 520 billion won in sales to foreign customers. The flagship store has expanded Korean fashion offerings and themed events to attract overseas visitors. Foreign customer sales at its Jamsil complex in eastern Seoul doubled from a year earlier. Shoppers from North America and Europe accounted for 35 percent of foreign sales there, up 15 percent from 2019. Growth also extended beyond Seoul. Sales to foreign shoppers at its Busan stores rose 150 percent from the previous year, while those at stores in the country’s southwestern region, including Jeonju and Gwangju, doubled during the same period, according to the company. item.title: Samsung Electro-Mechanics lands $210 mil. MLCC supply deal
item.description: Samsung Electro-Mechanics has secured a $210.24 million (282 billion won) order to supply multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) to a global company, adding to a string of large deals driven by growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) server components, the company said Tuesday in a regulatory filing. The company signed the one-year supply contract, which runs from Jan. 1 through Dec. 31, 2027. The customer was not disclosed due to a confidentiality agreement. The latest deal represents 2.5 percent of Samsung Electro-Mechanics’ total sales last year. It brings the value of the company’s major supply contracts announced this year to nearly 4 trillion won, which includes contracts not subject to disclosure. MLCCs regulate electrical current and reduce electromagnetic interference in electronic circuits. AI servers require more MLCCs than conventional servers and demand for the products goes higher under high-temperature and high-voltage conditions. item.title: Doosan Enerbility ships 1st gas turbine to US for SpaceXAI
item.description: Doosan Enerbility said Wednesday it has shipped a gas turbine to Space XAI for the U.S.-based artificial intelligence (AI) company's energy infrastructure project. The South Korean power plant builder said the DGT6-300H gas turbine was manufactured at its facility in the southeastern city of Changwon, marking the company's first gas turbine shipment to the United States. The turbine will be deployed as part of a U.S. energy infrastructure project by SpaceXAI, the AI arm of Elon Musk's SpaceX, according to the Korean company. Doosan Enerbility said it plans to expand cooperation with global technology companies amid growing demand for power generation equipment for AI infrastructure.

item.title: Korea has 52 death row inmates, average age of 58.7
item.description: With executions suspended in Korea for nearly 30 years, 52 death row inmates are currently being held in domestic correctional facilities, the justice ministry said Tuesday. The death row prisoners have an average age of 58.7, while 17, or 32.7 percent, are aged 60 or older, the ministry said, four days ahead of World Day Against the Death Penalty, observed annually on Oct. 10. Those in their 50s make up the largest group, with 29 inmates, it added. The death-sentenced prisoners include notorious serial killers Yoo Young-chul and Kang Ho-sun, who are currently imprisoned at the Seoul Detention Center after being convicted of killing 20 and 10 people, respectively. Korea has not carried out an execution for nearly 30 years, with the last execution taking place on Dec. 30, 1997, when 23 people, including members of the Jijonpa murder gang, were put to death in the final year of the Kim Young-sam administration. item.title: Astana AI Film Festival crowns winners, $450,000 Grand Prize goes to Latvia
item.description: Kazakhstan hosted the inaugural Astana AI Film Festival, drawing 8,067 entries from 125 countries and becoming the world’s largest international competition for artificial intelligence (AI)-generated films. The festival’s Grand Prix and $450,000 prize, equivalent to around 201.5 million tenge, went to Latvian filmmaker Nikolay Shestak for "The First Honest Day." Kazakhstan’s Myrzakhan Zhumakhan won the Best Character category for his comedy "It Was Just a Joke." The film follows a dog and its owner’s brother as they quarrel over a prank, with events unfolding like a blockbuster. Zhumakhan said he enjoys pranks and humor, which inspired him to create the story. The second-place award of $200,000, or about 89.5 million tenge, went to India’s "SITARA," while Spain’s "Looking For Perseida" took third place and $100,000, equivalent to around 44.8 million tenge. Only 25 films were selected from thousands of submissions to reach the final. item.title: Spy agency rejects media report on US visa denial for staff
item.description: Korea’s spy agency said Tuesday that it is in talks with the United States over delays in issuing visas to some of its employees scheduled to work at the Korean Embassy in Washington, denying a media report that their visa applications had been rejected. The statement from the National Intelligence Service (NIS) came in response to a Chosun Ilbo report revealing that the U.S. government had not approved Korea's request to dispatch NIS personnel to Washington as diplomats. The report also said Washington has not yet reached an agreement with Seoul over the departure of a senior NIS official who is supposed to return to Korea. “The delays in some visa applications are related to issues concerning the applicants’ personal information as part of the strengthened U.S. entry procedures,” the NIS said. “We are closely consulting with the U.S. side on the matter.” The intelligence agency further dismissed claims that the visa delays were linked to broader tensions between Seoul and Washington, including disputes over e-commerce giant Coupang and allegations involving intelligence act

item.title: Assembly speaker to embark on 4-nation trip to Europe
item.description: National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik was set to depart on a four-nation trip to Europe on Tuesday to discuss economic and industrial cooperation. Cho plans to visit Italy, Vatican City, Croatia and Greece over nine days on his first overseas trip since taking office in June. In Italy, he is scheduled to meet with Lorenzo Fontana, president of the country's Chamber of Deputies, and Gian Marco Centinaio, vice president of its Senate, on Wednesday to discuss expanding exchanges between the countries' parliaments and supporting economic and industrial cooperation. item.title: Gov't issues consumer alert, launches monthlong effort to prevent fraud after data breaches
item.description: Financial authorities issued a consumer alert at the “caution” level Tuesday after suspected artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cyberattacks stole personal information from banks, savings banks and a capital finance company. They also launched a monthlong special response period to prevent scams involving the stolen data. The measures follow data breaches reported at seven firms since the beginning of this month — Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, Hana Bank, BNK Busan Bank, Yegaram Savings Bank, Welcome Savings Bank and Hyundai Capital. The incidents suggest the attacks, first reported in the banking sector, are having a broader impact. During the special response period, financial firms must open dedicated support channels for affected customers and immediately report any confirmed or suspected cases of fraud that may follow to regulators. Firms must also strengthen monitoring through their fraud detection systems. item.description: A recent wave of cyberattacks on local banks is raising the stakes for an upcoming CEO reshuffle, with the heads of the country's five major lenders all set to see their terms expire at the end of the year, industry officials said Tuesday. The incidents, some of which involved artificial intelligence (AI), are expected to put banks' cybersecurity measures under greater scrutiny during this month's parliamentary audit and weigh on decisions over whether to reappoint incumbent chiefs. item.title: 'Reawaken Man: The Red' defies death, gravity in bold action gamble
item.description: "Reawaken Man: The Red" is action through and through. Koo Kyo-hwan, an actor who has moved fluidly across genres, takes on a new challenge by diving headfirst into action in "Reawaken Man: The Red." At a time when Korean action films have increasingly emphasized realistic combat and visceral impact, the film makes a bold choice by building its spectacle around a decidedly unrealistic premise: resurrection. Based on the popular webtoon of the same name, "Reawaken Man: The Red" follows Seok-hwan, played by Koo, an unemployed job seeker who discovers that he comes back to life 72 hours after dying. That extraordinary ability soon makes him the target of a relentless pursuit. The story builds on the idea that an ordinary man becomes increasingly powerful each time he dies and returns. At a relatively brisk 101 minutes, the film compresses its narrative into a fast-paced package that rarely slows down. Action is what gives the story much of that momentum. item.title: Robotic arms take over school kitchen duties in southern Seoul
item.description: The newest assistant in Seoul’s school kitchens doesn't take lunch breaks, doesn't mind the steam and automatically drains boiling grease after deep-frying. And according to local students, its cooking is a hit. Gangnam District in southern Seoul said Tuesday that its ongoing school meal robot program has undergone major upgrades based on feedback from school kitchen staff. The automated cooking system, first installed in August 2023 across three local schools — Gaeil Elementary, Gaewon Middle and Seoul Robotics High School — is proving that human-robot collaboration can transform high-stress workplaces. Originally launched as a pilot program with the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education and Korea Robotics — a local firm specializing in kitchen automation — the system pairs collaborative robotic arms with custom control software and heavy-duty cooking kettles. Rather than replacing kitchen staff, these mechanical assistants handle the most physically demanding tasks, from deep-frying to stirring large vats of soup and stir-fries. The safety improvements have been substantial

item.title: Hyundai Glovis, LGL explore SMR-powered car carrier route
item.description: Hyundai Glovis said Tuesday it has signed a memorandum of understanding with U.S.-based Liberty Global Logistics (LGL) to jointly explore operating a small modular reactor (SMR)-powered pure car and truck carrier (PCTC) between Korea and the United States. LGL specializes in transporting automobiles, heavy equipment, breakbulk and project cargo and is a major U.S. Department of Defense contractor for government cargo. The agreement was signed Sept. 30 at LGL's headquarters in Jericho, New York, with Kim Tae-woo, executive vice president of Hyundai Glovis' Logistics Business Division, and David Minetti, president of LGL, among the officials present from both companies. Hyundai Glovis will assess port conditions, regulations and operational requirements in Korea, while LGL will review the U.S. regulatory and operating environment. The companies will also study vessel development and construction, flag-state and classification requirements, and commercialization strategies. An SMR-powered vessel could enable long-term operations with minimal carbon emissions and without frequent refueling.

item.title: Seoul sent $2.4 bil. to Washington for Texas energy project: finance minister
item.description: Korea has transferred $2.4 billion to Washington as part of its funding for a Texas energy project agreed upon by the two countries under Seoul's investment initiative, the finance minister confirmed Tuesday. Responding to a lawmaker's question about whether the transfer had been made during a parliamentary audit, Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il replied "yes," acknowledging around 10 percent of the project's estimated budget was sent to the United States on Thursday. The gas-fired combined-cycle power plant project in Texas, dubbed "Project Star," calls for the construction of a 6,472-megawatt power plant for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers at a cost of $22.3 billion. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources recently announced three projects under Korea's investment pledge to the U.S., unveiled last year in return for lower tariffs. The pledge comprises $150 billion for shipbuilding cooperation and $200 billion for projects in various strategic sectors. item.title: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces expel Houthi rebels from several areas around key strait, officials say
item.description: ADEN, Yemen — Forces of the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen have recaptured several key areas around the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Iran-backed Houthi rebels , Yemeni officials said Monday, while the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi oil facilities, airports and military bases as fighting escalated on Yemen’s western coast. The Yemeni officials said forces allied with the internationally recognized government retook the crucial town of Dhubab just north of the strait, a vital shipping route that connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden. They also captured the towns of Bab and Hadeid, said the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to reporters. Witnesses said they saw government tanks and forces entering the towns. The government push came as part of a major offensive launched early Monday under air cover by a Saudi military coalition. Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, the Houthis' military spokesman, claimed in a pre-recorded statement that the rebels used ballistic and cruise missiles and drones in attacks targeting King Khali

item.title: Busan shark refuses to leave canal for 3 weeks despite rescue attempts
item.description: Nearly three weeks have passed as of Tuesday since a shark, now the most famous of its kind in Korea, got trapped in a canal at a waterfront park in the southeastern city of Busan, despite local authorities' rescue attempts. The shark was first spotted Sept. 18 in the narrow canal at the city's North Port, located some 330 kilometers south of Seoul. For the next two days, nearly 20,000 visitors came to see the shark, a fivefold increase compared with the park's usual daily average of about 2,000 visitors during holidays. Public interest spiked dramatically during the Chuseok holiday, which fell on Sept. 25, with a daily average of 120,750 visitors flocking to the waterfront park between Sept. 24 and Sept. 27. The shark has been affectionately named "Bukang-i" after Bukhang, or North Port, as well as serving as an honorary ambassador of Busan. As of Monday, 1.02 million people have visited the park to see Bukang-i, according to the Busan city government. item.title: Seoul unveils 2026 Gourmet 100 list to map out capital's best bites
item.description: From hidden neighborhood eateries to trendy dessert spots, Seoul is offering international travelers a curated path through its culinary scene with the launch of its 2026 Gourmet 100 guide and an expanded citywide food festival. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday that 100 restaurants and food establishments were selected across seven categories — Korean, Western, Asian, grill, vegetarian, cafe and dessert, and bars and pubs — by a panel of 60 Korean food experts. The list, launched in 2020, includes 27 Korean food establishments, 23 Western, 15 Asian, 10 grill, eight vegetarian, nine cafe and dessert, and eight bar and pub venues, with 25 newcomers this year. The 2026 selection organizes Seoul’s culinary landscape into distinct categories, spanning traditional Korean fine dining, Western cuisine, Asian flavors, Grill establishments, Plant-Based eateries, Bars & Pubs, and a newly expanded Cafe & Dessert section. item.title: FM Cho says S. Korea reviewing diplomatic responses to NK mine blast inside DMZ
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Tuesday that South Korea is reviewing various diplomatic measures in response to recent mine explosions inside the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), while seeking to prevent the situation from escalating unnecessarily. Cho made the remarks during a parliamentary audit of his ministry, a day after the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) concluded that North Korean land mines planted south of the Military Demarcation Line (MDL) caused injuries to three South Korean soldiers inside the DMZ on Sept. 21. "We take this matter very seriously. Based on the final results of the investigation, the ministry is reviewing various things it can do and will work with the National Security Council to formulate the government's response," Cho said. The blasts occurred while South Korean troops were clearing a path for a joint inspection with the U.N. Command (UNC) to verify suspicions that Pyongyang had illegally planted land mines south of the border in violation of the Armistice Agreement that ended the 1950-53 Korean War. item.title: California scientist wins a Nobel Prize, then makes school lunches for his kids
item.description: STANFORD, Calif. — Dr. Karl Deisseroth spent hours fielding congratulatory calls after learning early Monday that he had won a Nobel Prize for medicine for helping to open a new field of brain science called optogenetics. But it wasn't long before the California scientist asked for a break from all the attention for a more ordinary task: He needed to make school lunches for his children, who were asleep in the family home in Stanford, where their father had been speaking in the middle of the night with journalists and well-wishers. Deisseroth, 54, shared this year’s medicine prize with two researchers in Germany for their work in optogenetics, a field that combines light with genes to switch on and off neurons in living brains. A self-described night owl, the Howard Hughes Medical Institute investigator and Stanford University professor often works past midnight. After reviewing papers and emailing his students, he said he had just gone to lie down when he got the call from the Nobel Assembly in Stockholm. “I almost felt as if I’d lost the power of forming words,” he told The A

item.title: What to know about suspected bomb plot against UK air base used by US in Iran war
item.description: LONDON — The U.S. has withdrawn its bombers stationed at a U.S.-run military air base in England used to strike Iran, as police investigate whether a suspected terror plot at the base is linked to Iran. Five men were detained shortly after midnight on Sept. 27 on suspected explosives and terrorism offenses after three suspicious vans were spotted traveling toward RAF Fairford. The U.K.-owned base has been used by American bombers during decades of conflicts in the Middle East, including the ongoing Iran war. A sixth suspect, a British-Iranian dual national, was arrested several days later. All the men have been released on bail. Police earlier said they did not find any explosives in the vans that sparked the security alert. The developments have led to confusion about what exactly happened at the air base. British authorities have linked the incident to Tehran. Iran has denied involvement. item.title: 'China has never asked Seoul to choose a side between Beijing, Washington,' envoy says
item.description: As competition between the United States and China increasingly extends from diplomacy to technology and supply chains, Seoul faces the challenge of managing ties with its security ally and one of its most important economic partners. Chinese Ambassador to Korea Dai Bing said Seoul does not need to choose between Washington and Beijing, saying maintaining relations with both countries serves Korea’s national interests. “China has never asked Korea to choose a side between China and the United States,” Dai said in an interview with The Korea Times in Seoul, Sept. 29. “We hope that Korea will pursue sound relations parallel with both China and the United States, guided by its own fundamental national interests.” The ambassador said U.S.-China competition should not be the sole lens through which the regional order in East Asia is viewed, adding China hopes Korea will pursue what he described as “genuine strategic autonomy.” Dai emphasized that strategic autonomy does not mean giving up Korea’s alliance with the U.S., saying China respects the alliance relationship based on

item.title: Nexon partners with Chernin Entertainment to bring ARC Raiders, The Finals to screen
item.description: Nexon has signed a partnership with Hollywood production company Chernin Entertainment to develop film and television adaptations of its video games ARC Raiders and The Finals, the Tokyo-listed game company said Tuesday. Under the deal, Chernin Entertainment will lead the development of film and TV projects based on the two titles, both made by Embark Studios, Nexon's Stockholm-based subsidiary. Financial terms and release schedules were not disclosed. ARC Raiders is a survival action game set on a post-apocalyptic Earth ruled by machines called ARC, in which players scavenge for resources while fighting both the machines and one another. Released last October, it drew 700,000 concurrent players across all platforms within two weeks and has since sold more than 16 million copies worldwide, Nexon said. The game won best multiplayer game at The Game Awards, Online Game of the Year at the D.I.C.E. Awards and the multiplayer prize at the BAFTA Games Awards. item.title: IVE, Illit, RIIZE collide as October K-pop comeback race heats up
item.description: The Asian Games and the Chuseok holiday have come and gone, and the air has finally turned crisp with the arrival of autumn, but K-pop's race to the top of the charts is running as hot as ever. October brings more than a dozen notable releases, building to a single day on Oct. 26 when three of the industry's biggest names put out new music at once. Before then, the calendar fills with quick returns from rising groups, a virtual idol act fresh off its first stadium show and a new solo EP from BLACKPINK's Lisa. Early-month rush KickFlip, one of JYP Entertainment's youngest boy groups, returns on Tuesday with the mini album "KICK OFF THE WALL Pt. 1," about six months after "My First Kick" in April. The eight-track album is led by the double title tracks "Puzzle Piece" and "Kick Off The Wall," featuring U.S. rapper iann dior, with every member taking part in writing all the songs. Oct. 12 is the month's first crowded evening. NCT WISH of SM Entertainment releases its fourth mini album, "I SPY," with six tracks led by the title track of the same name. item.title: LG Uplus, Woori Bank team up to spot voice phishing calls in real time
item.description: Mobile carrier LG Uplus has partnered with Woori Bank to feed real-time scam alerts to the lender, helping block fraudulent wire transfers while victims are still on the line with voice phishing scammers. Voice phishing refers to phone scams in which callers pose as prosecutors, police or bank employees to trick victims into transferring money. Under the service, ixi-O, the mobile carrier's artificial intelligence (AI)-powered call app, flags a suspicious call and sends the risk information to the bank. Woori Bank then steps up monitoring of the customer through its fraud detection system, which screens transactions for abnormal patterns. If a suspicious transaction follows, the bank will take protective steps under its internal procedures, such as additional identity verification or a notice to the customer, LG Uplus said. The company said banks' anti-phishing efforts have focused on transaction data such as account transfers, making it difficult to catch warning signs before money moves. item.title: Jeju Air ramps up China routes ahead of winter travel surge
item.description: Jeju Air will add flights on four China routes this winter and has secured rights to launch services from Incheon to Beijing and Changsha, the Korean low-cost carrier said Tuesday. The airline said it was allocated traffic rights in September for seven weekly Incheon-Beijing flights and four weekly Incheon-Changsha flights. Traffic rights are government-issued permits that set how often a carrier may fly an international route. In April, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport awarded it rights on five other routes: Busan-Guilin, Busan-Shanghai, Daegu-Shanghai, Jeju-Chengdu and Jeju-Chongqing. The allocations allow Jeju Air to serve 13 Chinese cities, the most among Korean low-cost carriers, the company said. It currently operates 14 China routes, including nonscheduled services. Changsha, the capital of Hunan province, is a gateway to Zhangjiajie, a mountain area known for its sandstone pillars. item.title: Jongmyo Shrine, Basilica of Saint-Denis exchange French, Korean visitor guides
item.description: Situated nearly 5,500 miles apart, Seoul’s Jongmyo Shrine and the Basilica Cathedral of Saint-Denis near Paris share a remarkably similar historic duty: serving as the final resting places for two nations' royal dynasties. Now, the two historic sites are swapping native languages to welcome an expanding influx of international travelers. Officials from Korea’s Royal Palaces and Tombs Center met with France’s Centre des Monuments Nationaux inside the Saint-Denis cathedral last week to officially exchange freshly published visitor guidebooks — offering French text for Jongmyo and Korean for Saint-Denis. The initiative marks the first concrete deliverable under a cultural collaboration agreement signed during a bilateral summit in April. Both institutions sought to deepen diplomatic and heritage ties by linking their premier royal burial sites. Jongmyo Shrine, built in 1395, houses the spirit tablets of Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910) kings and queens. item.title: SKT showcases AI battlefield command tools at Army festival
item.description: SK Telecom, Korea’s largest wireless telecommunications operator, was the lone private-sector company at Korea’s Ground Forces Festival, where it spent five days showcasing artificial intelligence (AI) and communications technologies designed to reshape how military commanders gather information, make decisions and stay connected in contested environments. SKT said Tuesday that it participated in the festival from Thursday to Monday at Gyeryongdae airfield in Gyeryong, South Chungcheong Province, presenting AI defense transformation technologies under its T military brand. The centerpiece was its AI staff system, which combines a data platform, ontology technology and digital twins to connect battlefield information and help commanders assess situations and make tactical decisions. The system is designed to bring together data generated by troops and equipment, as well as drones, robots and sensors, then deliver relevant information quickly enough to support faster decisions. Visitors and military officials could follow the process from data collection and analysis to digital battlef

item.title: 28 IP addresses behind recent hacking attacks against Korean financial institutions: watchdog
item.description: The country's financial watchdog has pinpointed 28 internet protocol (IP) addresses in the United States, Japan and 10 other countries used for a series of recent hacking attacks Korean financial institutions, industry sources said Tuesday. Several financial companies, including Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank, suffered back-to-back leaks of customer information in recent hacking attacks last week, raising concerns that more firms might have suffered data breaches. According to the sources, the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) has shortlisted IP addresses in 12 countries as of 6:00 p.m. on Monday, which are presumed to have been used for the artificial intelligence (AI) agent-backed hacking. But it has not been able to pinpoint the locations of some of the IP addresses, they said. Local financial firms have been in a hurry to check their own security systems to fend off any additional hacking attempts. item.title: LG CNS unveils blockchain tech to help banks issue stablecoins, tokens
item.description: LG CNS launched a blockchain infrastructure platform designed to help financial institutions build services around stablecoins, tokenized securities and real-world assets as Korea’s financial sector moves toward broader use of digital assets. The information technology services giant said Tuesday that its new platform, called KITL, provides four core functions: digital wallets, transaction processing, fee payment and transaction data collection. KITL is designed to address infrastructure needs that arise when financial institutions handle assets on public blockchains, where transactions occur outside systems directly controlled by banks, securities firms and other service providers. Its wallet system can generate private keys only when signatures are required and discard them afterward, allowing institutions to issue wallets at large scale without continuously expanding hardware security module capacity, the company said. item.title: 2026 Genesis GV80 Hybrid pairs twin-turbo V6 with EV-style torque
item.description: Genesis has entered Korea’s rear-wheel-drive hybrid luxury SUV market with the launch of the GV80 Hybrid, pairing a 2.5-liter turbo engine with an electric motor system designed to deliver stronger performance, improved fuel economy and a quieter ride. Genesis, Hyundai Motor Group’s luxury brand, began selling the GV80 Hybrid on Tuesday, marking its first model to use a rear-wheel-drive-based 2.5 turbo hybrid system. The SUV produces a combined 352 horsepower, about 16 percent more than the 304 horsepower offered by the 2.5 turbo gasoline model, while achieving combined fuel economy of 12 kilometers per liter in the 19-inch, two-wheel-drive, five-seat configuration. GV80 Hybrid uses a parallel hybrid system combining a P1 starter motor and a P2 drive motor capable of producing up to 59.1 kilowatts, with the latter handling propulsion and regenerative braking. Genesis said its new seven-speed transmission improves power delivery efficiency and allows the vehicle to reverse using the P2 motor without engine assistance. item.title: Lee orders dedication of personnel, resources to handling hacking attacks
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung instructed the government Tuesday to dedicate personnel and resources to minimizing damage from a recent series of hacking attacks at financial firms. Lee gave the order at a Cabinet meeting in response to revelations that the attacks exposed customer information at seven companies, including Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank. "In some hacking cases, details have emerged of the possible use of artificial intelligence (AI), causing the people to feel great concern and anxiety," he said. "Please carry out a swift and clear determination of the circumstances and concentrate personnel and resources on minimizing damage." Police said the same day that an investigation has been launched into the cyber attacks, with a 28-member team looking into charges of violations of the information and communications network law. Lee called for high vigilance not only within the government and business sectors but across society, saying AI-driven hacking methods are increasing the scope of damage to previously unseen levels. item.title: Unification ministry vows dialogue over hard-line response to DMZ blast
item.description: The unification ministry said Tuesday it will keep seeking peaceful solutions to inter-Korean issues, reiterating its commitment to seeking dialogue following the recent explosions of North Korea-planted land mines inside the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) that injured three South Korean military officers. The statement came a day after Seoul's defense ministry concluded North Korea was behind the Sept. 21 land mine explosions. The ministry said it would consider the next steps with relevant government agencies, including the defense ministry. "We will keep working to break the vicious cycle of hostility and confrontation, and to build a virtuous cycle of peace and prosperity," it said, adding it would pursue lasting peace "through communication rather than a hard-line standoff." The South Korean military on Monday announced the final results of its joint investigation with the U.N. Command into the blast, confirming its preliminary findings that resin antipersonnel mines deliberately planted by Pyongyang south of the Military Demarcation Line caused the explosion. item.title: S. Korea, US aligned on N. Korea policy, denuclearization of Korean Peninsula: FM Cho
item.description: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Tuesday that South Korea and the United States are aligned in their North Korea policy and remain committed to the goal of denuclearizing the Korean Peninsula. "Through multiple summit meetings, South Korea and the U.S. have confirmed their aligned policy stance toward North Korea and their commitment to coordination," Cho said during a parliamentary audit of the foreign ministry. "We have continued close consultations with the U.S. to encourage North Korea to return to dialogue and negotiations," he said, vowing continued efforts to encourage "constructive roles from China and Russia." The minister stressed the government's commitment to seeking "substantive progress" on the North Korean nuclear issue through a phased and practical approach aimed at halting, reducing and eventually dismantling its nuclear capabilities. item.title: Nuri rocket readies for 5th launch
item.description: Korea’s homegrown Nuri rocket completed preparations for liftoff on Tuesday, a day before its fifth launch, scheduled for around noon. According to the Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA), Nuri arrived at the launchpad at the Naro Space Center in Goheung, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City, around 7:40 a.m. and was erected and secured at 10:30 a.m. KASA plans to hold its launch management committee around 8:45 a.m. Wednesday to finalize the launch time. Liftoff is planned between 12:23 p.m. and 1:30 p.m., with the flight expected to last about 30 minutes. The fifth launch is intended to build Nuri’s reliability through repeated production and launches using the same design, while placing its largest-ever number of satellites into orbit. Since the fourth launch last year, Hanwha Aerospace has been overseeing the production and assembly process as the rocket’s system integrator. The Nuri will carry 15 satellites on its fifth launch: five NEONSAT swarm microsatellites as the primary payload and 10 CubeSats as secondary payloads. The total payload weight is about 1,071 kilogra

item.title: Gov't honors pioneers who shaped Korea's alphabet and spread it globally
item.description: Long before digital typography defined everyday communication across smartphones and computer screens in East Asia, Korea relied heavily on imported Japanese typesetting. That changed when Seok Geum-ho founded Sandoll, pioneering an industry that produced more than 1,000 distinct Korean fonts over four decades and permanently altered the visual identity of the modern written language. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Tuesday that the late font designer will posthumously receive the Eungwan Order of Cultural Merit, Korea’s top cultural honor, on Friday during the upcoming 580th Hangul Day national ceremony at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts in Seoul. The annual awards recognize eight individuals and two organizations for significant contributions to the development, research, and international growth of Hangeul, the Korean alphabet created in 1443 by King Sejong the Great to promote popular literacy. Joining Seok among top honorees is Baek Tae-hyeon, vice president of Korean Institute in Central Asia, who will receive the Okgwan Order of Cultural Merit. Baek s

item.title: Actor Park Bo-gum turns palace sounds into new Korean travel experience
item.description: Actor Park Bo-gum led a group of roughly 100 international visitors on a soundscape walking tour at Changgyeong Palace earlier this month, spearheading a campaign by cultural authorities to shift tourism promotion toward sensory travel. Organized by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism alongside the Korea Tourism Organization, the "Korea Sound Journey" event brought together travelers and content creators selected from more than 2,300 applicants across 20 countries, including the United States, China, Japan and Thailand. The initiative directly expands on the country's 2026 global advertising campaign, "Begin to Hear Korea," which launched in July. Starring Park — serving his second consecutive year as Korea's honorary tourism ambassador — the promotional series features the actor alongside a Danish musician traveling across the peninsula to record intimate, everyday soundscapes. item.title: Foreign visitors to Seoul up 22% through August
item.description: The number of foreign visitors to Seoul in the first eight months of this year increased by about 22 percent from the same period last year, while their credit card spending in the city surged nearly 60 percent, data from the city government showed Tuesday. Seoul attracted a record 11.56 million foreign tourists in the January to August period, up 21.6 percent from a year earlier, the government said, noting their credit card spending surged 59.9 percent year-on-year to 7.78 trillion won ($5.8 billion). In August alone, 1.72 million foreign visitors visited the capital, up 23.3 percent from 1.4 million a year earlier, it noted. By country, tourists from China, Japan and Taiwan accounted for 66.4 percent of foreign visitors to Seoul in August. China topped the list with 636,000 visitors (36.9 percent), followed by Japan with 322,000 (18.6 percent) and Taiwan with 188,000 (10.9 percent). item.title: Defense chief says mine-removal operation a 'decisive' response against N. Korea
item.description: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul said Tuesday the mine-clearing operation conducted at the site of a recent blast inside the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) was a "decisive" response against North Korea, noting it marked the first such mission inside the buffer zone between the two Koreas. Kang made the remarks a day after the South Korean military announced the final result of a joint investigation with the U.N. Command (UNC) into the Sept. 21 mine blast that left three South Korean soldiers injured. The joint probe concluded that antipersonnel mines deliberately planted by North Korean troops south of the Military Demarcation Line (MDL) were the cause of the explosion. item.title: Former press secretary Karoline Leavitt lands her next gig: Fox News contributor
item.description: NEW YORK — Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt has found her next chapter: She is heading to Fox News. Leavitt will serve as an on-air contributor beginning Nov. 1, the network said Monday. “Karoline’s firsthand experience in the White House and on the presidential campaign trail gives her a distinct understanding of today’s political landscape,” said the network’s CEO, Suzanne Scott. For her part, Leavitt, in the same statement, said she looked forward “to bringing my unique perspective from my experience as White House Press Secretary, along with the same energy and candor that defined my tenure, to Fox’s millions of viewers across their many platforms.” Leavitt, now 29, was the youngest person to hold the role of press secretary. When she left at the end of August, President Donald Trump described her as one of his “most trusted aides.” At the time she said she wanted to spend more time with her two children. Her second child, Viviana, was born in May, and she has a two-year-old son. Leavitt is not the first of Trump's press secretaries to join Fox

item.title: MiCo chairman wins top US ceramic industry award
item.description: MiCo Group Chairman Jeon Seon-kyu has received a top honor from the American Ceramic Society (ACerS) for his leadership in advancing ceramic technology, the company said Tuesday. Jeon was presented with the Medal for Leadership in the Advancement of Ceramic Technology at ACerS’ Annual Honors & Awards Banquet on Monday (local time) in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The award recognizes senior industry executives who have demonstrated leadership and vision in driving corporate growth and advancing the ceramic industry. Up to two recipients are selected each year, one from the Americas and one from outside the region. Jeon was the sole recipient this year. Jeon is the first Korean to receive the award. In Asia, only four Japanese and two Chinese recipients have previously been selected. ACerS recognized Jeon for MiCo Group’s development of advanced ceramic technologies used at major semiconductor manufacturing sites worldwide. It also highlighted the group’s efforts to develop core ceramic materials, localize key components for semiconductor manufacturing equipment and establish mass-produc

item.title: Hearts2Hearts releases Korean version of Japanese debut single 'Iconic Heart'
item.description: Girl group Hearts2Hearts released a Korean-language version of "Iconic Heart," the title track of its first Japanese single, on Monday, its agency SM Entertainment said. "Iconic Heart (Korean Ver.)" is available on major streaming platforms, about two months after the original came out in Japan on Aug. 12. The song is a dance track inspired by Jersey club, a fast-paced style of club music that originated in the U.S. state of New Jersey, and is built around bright synthesizers and bouncy beats. Its lyrics convey the excitement of moving forward together through playful, youthful imagery, according to SM, one of Korea's largest K-pop agencies and home to acts such as aespa and NCT. The agency said the Korean version offers a new take on the track while keeping the energy of the original. The group first performed the Korean version Friday at Spotify Closer, a concert held in partnership with the music streaming service in Seoul's Yeongdeungpo District. Spotify launched the series to spotlight Korean artists. Hearts2Hearts was its first featured act. Hearts2Hearts plans to promote the single

item.title: 'I Live Alone' viewers captivated by actor who lives in 90-year-old home
item.description: Actor Kim Min has won praise from viewers after revealing his unconventional daily life and personal philosophy on MBC's reality show "I Live Alone." Beyond the intensity he has shown in acting roles, Kim displayed a free-spirited side as he filled his days with home repairs, martial arts and hands-on projects. But it was his outlook on life — particularly his belief that being "cool" comes from how a person spends their time rather than their looks — that resonated most with viewers. The Oct. 2 episode of "I Live Alone" offered a glimpse into Kim's life in Dongducheon, Gyeonggi Province, where he has lived alone for 28 years. He resides in a roughly 90-year-old house whose distinctive atmosphere and unconventional setup immediately drew attention. Kim began his day by running a generator for electricity and tearing into an entire baguette. He repaired a damaged floor himself with cement, worked on woodworking projects and practiced martial arts. Despite living in surroundings that might seem inconvenient to others, Kim appeared perfectly at ease, making and repairing what he needed

item.title: Sogang University selected for government-led AI training project
item.description: Sogang University is stepping up efforts to foster professionals capable of driving the artificial intelligence (AI) transformation of the manufacturing industry under a government-led initiative. The university said it has been selected for the AI innovation skills development project, which is promoted by the Ministry of Science and ICT and administered by the Institute of Information & Communications Technology Planning & Evaluation (IITP). Cho Sung-in, a professor in the university’s Department of Artificial Intelligence, will lead the project. Under the project, the university will receive 16.25 billion won ($12 million) in government funding over five years and five months through December 2031. The university plans to nurture master’s- and doctoral-level students capable of understanding manufacturing processes and developing AI models, as well as applying and validating them in industrial settings. A university official said the project calls for nurturing AI transformation students capable of shaping the future of Korea’s manufacturing industry through cyber-physical proces

item.title: KickFlip takes bold step forward with 'Kick Off The Wall'
item.description: Emerging K-pop powerhouse KickFlip is shedding its "rookie" label to step onto the global stage. Returning from a six-month hiatus, all seven members took a hands-on approach to their new mini-album, "KICK OFF THE WALL Pt. 1." Anchored by a feature from American singer-songwriter iann dior on the title track, "Kick Off The Wall," alongside co-lead "Incomplete," the release delivers a story of confronting uncertainty and forging your own path. Packed with energetic performances, personal songwriting and a bold crossover sound, KickFlip is betting on its most ambitious project yet to prove its reach extends far beyond Korea. To dig deeper into how this new direction came together, the band sat down to discuss the creative journey behind the music. Q. You are returning about six months after “My First Kick,” so how do you feel about this comeback? KickFlip: We’re excited to show many new sides of ourselves, starting with our first double title tracks, and we’re looking forward to sharing the album with everyone. Q. What story did you want to tell through “KICK OFF THE WALL Pt. 1”

item.title: Finance minister vows efforts to tame inflation, boost growth
item.description: Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il on Tuesday vowed to focus on taming inflation to ease the cost-of-living burden while boosting economic growth through major government-led initiatives, including the three megaprojects. Lee made the remarks during a parliamentary audit by the finance, economy, planning and budget committee at the National Assembly, stressing his priorities are aimed at improving people's livelihoods and addressing economic disparities. It was Lee's first parliamentary audit session since taking office last month. "We will maintain consumer price stability, which is the foundation of people's livelihoods," the policymaker said. Lee added the finance ministry will focus particularly on stabilizing the prices of everyday necessities, such as fuel and food. "We will take stern action against irregular activities disrupting market prices and make efforts to ease the financial burdens on vulnerable groups," Lee said. item.title: Watchdog unveils guidelines on deceptive 'dark patterns' on online platforms
item.description: Korea's fair trade watchdog on Tuesday released guidelines for online platforms to avoid "dark patterns," or deceptive practices designed to make it difficult for users to cancel subscriptions or induce them to make irrational purchases. The Fair Trade Commission (FTC) said the latest guidelines consolidate and update existing guidance and provide detailed examples of violations to help platform operators comply with the rules. Dark patterns refer to practices that trick consumers into making payments or signing up for services without fully understanding what they are agreeing to. Examples include enrolling consumers in monthly subscription services without their knowledge or making cancellations difficult. Under the guidelines, platform operators are advised to place cancellation links in easily accessible locations, such as the website's homepage or sections accessible from it, including "My Account," rather than in less intuitive locations, such as "Security Settings." item.title: Nat'l Assembly kicks off annual audit of gov't agencies
item.description: The National Assembly launched its annual audit of government agencies Tuesday, with rival parties clashing over the Supreme Court chief's refusal to recommend a new justice nominee to the president and the recently publicized transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) from Ukraine. Eight of the Assembly's 17 standing committees opened their sessions starting at 10 a.m. on the first day of the audit, scheduled to run through Oct. 27. During the audit of the legislation and judiciary committee, lawmakers mainly wrangled over Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae's refusal to recommend a new candidate for court justice as requested by the presidential office. Earlier in August, the presidential office asked Cho to recommend a new candidate after taking issue with his written recommendation of two Supreme Court justice nominees to President Lee Jae Myung. Cho rejected the request, citing a lack of constitutional grounds to do so. item.title: US warns foreign financial institutions not to do business with Iran
item.description: WASHINGTON — The United States on Monday warned foreign financial institutions that if they conducted any business with Iran or its banking sector they could be sanctioned by Washington. "Foreign financial institutions continuing to transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions could be targeted at any time without advance notification and should take immediate action to terminate such activity and relationships," the US Treasury said in an "alert" statement. The United States launched its war against Iran in late February, killing the country's leadership and demanding it cease any nuclear-related activities. The war has plunged the Middle East into violence, with Tehran's retaliatory action targeting Washington's Gulf allies and sending global energy and fertilizer prices skyrocketing after it virtually shut a key trading route. Since late August, Washington has stepped up its campaign to economically isolate Tehran, warning its allies that they would be hit by secondary sanctions if they continued to conduct transactions with the country's government. item.title: PM calls for sweeping overhaul of information security systems following wave of cyberattacks
item.description: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook called Tuesday for a sweeping overhaul of the country's information protection system, warning that recent cyberattacks on major financial institutions show that current security measures are no longer effective. Several financial firms suffered back-to-back leaks of customer information in the recent attacks, including on Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank. President Lee Jae Myung has said the issue should be taken seriously and called for a thorough investigation. On Tuesday, the prime minister presided over a meeting with related ministers to discuss the issue. "This is a serious situation because this incident is believed to have taken advantage of artificial intelligence, and if AI is used in phishing attacks, it could lead to secondary damage," Han said. "It is also a serious situation in that similar hacking methods could spread beyond the financial sector to industries, as well as government and public sectors." item.title: Police launch probe into recent cyber attacks at financial firms
item.description: Police have launched an investigation into a recent series of cyber attacks against financial companies, officials said Tuesday. Several financial companies, including Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank, suffered back-to-back leaks of customer information in recent hacking attacks. The National Office of Investigation (NOI) said it has formed a 28-member team to investigate the case on suspicion of violations of the information and communications network law. Officials are also reviewing whether the case should be sent to the newly launched Serious Crime Investigation Agency, which handles cyber crimes against key state facilities and hacks into electronic financial infrastructure. "(We) will carry out an investigation swiftly and strictly while closely cooperating with relevant agencies to ease the public's anxiety," the NOI said.

item.title: N. Korea reviews Q3 economy, discusses yearly goals in Cabinet meeting
item.description: North Korea has held an enlarged Cabinet meeting via video conference to review its third-quarter economic performances, state media reported Tuesday. The meeting, presided over by Premier Pak Thae-song on Monday, also discussed ways to meet the year's economic targets, according to the Rodong Sinmun, the country's most widely read state newspaper. Officials reviewed the key goals set at the Ninth Congress of the Workers' Party of Korea, held in February, which laid out a new five-year plan through 2030 that stressed economic growth and self-reliance. According to the report, Vice Premier Kim Tok-hun said, "Remarkable progress has been made, and the foundation for self-reliant economy has been reinforced." He also called on officials to shed a "passive and risk-averse" work attitude to overcome "defects and bias" found in carrying out economic policy. The meeting, in particular, called for production drives in electricity, coal, agriculture and construction. item.title: Seoul shares end lower on tech losses amid rising bond yields
item.description: Seoul shares ended lower Tuesday, led by declines in technology stocks, amid concerns over rising bond yields at multidecade highs. The Korean won rose against the U.S. dollar. After opening higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) turned lower to close down 62.35 points, or 0.89 percent, at 6,941.39. Trade volume was light at 257.27 million shares worth 19.1 trillion won ($14.2 billion), with decliners outnumbering gainers 459 to 424. Foreigners and institutions sold a net 1.75 trillion won and 1.98 billion won worth of stocks, respectively. Individuals bought a net 740.56 billion won. Investors now await third-quarter corporate earnings, with higher interest rates, elevated energy costs and renewed inflation worries pushing up global bond yields. Investors are expected to remain cautious until there is a fresh policy catalyst or strong corporate earnings results, analysts said. In Seoul, tech stocks led the decline. Market bellwether Samsung Electronics fell 1.45 percent to 272,000 won, and its chipmaking rival SK hynix declined 3.69 percent to 1.77 million won. Kore

item.title: Busan film fest kicks off with 'A-list' status for 1st time
item.description: BUSAN — The 31st edition of the Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) begins its 10-day run Tuesday, with the festival seeking to bolster its global presence with its first "A-list" accreditation by a prominent global organization of filmmakers. This year's event will run through Oct. 15 in the southeastern South Korean city of Busan with 247 official selections from 59 nations, which marks the biggest slate since 2019, according to organizers. Of the total, 95 films will have their world premieres at BIFF. It marks the first time the event is taking place after the International Federation of Film Producers Associations selected BIFF as one of its 17 A-list festivals, alongside prestigious film fests, such as Cannes, Berlin and Venice. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences has also added BIFF to the list of six film fests where the top winner of the Busan Award will be eligible for submission to the Oscars in the Best International Feature Film category. item.title: Hyosung Chairman Cho Hyun-Joon completes bio-spandex base in Vietnam
item.description: Hyosung TNC, the world’s largest spandex maker by market share, has launched an integrated production system in Vietnam connecting sugarcane-based bio materials to finished textile products. The investment, carried out under the leadership of Hyosung Chairman Cho Hyun-joon, is aimed at reducing reliance on fossil fuel-based raw materials while internalizing the entire supply chain, from raw materials to finished products, to strengthen the company’s presence in the global sustainable textile market. Hyosung TNC said it recently began commercial operations at its Bio-Butanediol plant in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, with an annual production capacity of 50,000 tons. Backed by a total investment of $1 billion, the facility can expand its annual production capacity to 200,000 tons depending on future market growth. BDO is a raw material used in spandex production and has traditionally been produced using petrochemical resources such as coal. item.title: 'Yoon trauma' shapes battle over new investigative chief
item.description: The row over Kim Ji-yong’s nomination as the first head of the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency (SCIA) ostensibly centers on his record as a prosecutor, including allegations that he was aligned with Yoon Suk Yeol, a former prosecutor-turned-president. But the deeper issue may be anxiety within the ruling camp that the new investigative body, despite being created to separate investigation from prosecution, could operate beyond the government’s control and give rise to another Yoon-like political figure. That concern is rooted in the political aftershock of Yoon’s rise. As prosecutor general under the liberal Moon Jae-in government, he gained national prominence through investigations involving figures close to the president. His clashes with the administration helped turn him into a symbol of resistance to political power — an image that later became a key asset in his successful presidential campaign. For the ruling camp, that episode showed how one investigator can turn legal authority and high-profile cases into political capital. The separation of investigative and prose

item.title: Lawsuit accuses Starbucks of mislabeling 8 'sugar-free' protein drinks
item.description: Starbucks is facing a consumer lawsuit over claims that the protein drinks labeled “sugar-free” on its cafe menus may actually contain more sugar than a Reese’s peanut butter cup. The federal lawsuit filed late Friday in Seattle alleges that eight protein beverages Starbucks sells in the U.S. contain varying amounts of sugar even though the company lists them as sugarless. On Monday, the menu on Starbucks' U.S. website listed a 16-ounce (0.5-liter) Sugar-Free Caramel Protein Matcha with 16 grams of sugar and a 20-ounce (0.6-liter) version of the same drink with 21 grams of sugar. By comparison, one Reese’s cup has 11 grams of sugar. Hagens Berman, a law firm that specializes in class action cases, filed the suit on behalf of three individual consumers who bought Starbucks’ sugar-free protein drinks in California, New York and Washington. “Consumers avoid sugar for various reasons, whether that be general health, diabetes and blood glucose levels or other factors, and for many, a staunch mislabeling like this is significant,” said Steve Berman, a co-founder and managing part
